newsitem.title: USA: Duke Power, PanEnergy merger done.
newsitem.headline: Duke Power, PanEnergy merger done.

text.p: Duke Power Co and PanEnergy Corp said Wednesday they completed their previously announced merger and are now operating as Duke Energy Corp.

The merger called for each share of Houston-based PanEnergy to be converted into 1.0444 shares of Duke Energy stock, they said. Duke Power shareholders need take no action as Duke Power shares will represent Duke Energy shares.
Duke Energy said it will continue to trade under Duke Power's symbol on the New York Stock Exchange.

The $7.7 billion merger fuses PanEnergy's natural gas pipeline and services businesses with Duke Power's electric operations, creating a company with annual revenues greater than $12 billion, assets of $20 billon and a worldwide workforce of 22,000 people.
Duke Energy will be divided into four divisions, the company said. Its Duke Power unit will remain anchored in Charlotte, serving 1.8 million customers in the Carolinas.

Duke's Energy Services unit, housed in Houston, will offer a range of energy products and services to U.S. and international markets, including electricity and natural gas marketing; plant construction, operation and investment; and engineering and energy services consulting.

The company's Energy Transmission unit, also in Houston, will provide access to major domestic natural gas supply basins through its pipeline network to markets in the Midwest, Mid-Atlantic and Northeast states.

The Diversified Operations unit, based in Charlotte, wll handle non-energy related activities, including Crescent Resources Inc, a realty company, and DukeNet Communications, a telecommunications business.
